newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says U.N. Afghan talks shifted to Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says U.N. Afghan talks shifted to Geneva.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday a planned U.N. conference on aid for war-torn Afghanistan had been shifted to Switzerland after Islamabad objected to participation by arch rival India.

The meeting had been scheduled for December 2-3 in the northwestern Pakistan town of Peshawar by the U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Assistance to Afghanistan in cooperation with the U.N. Development Programme and and other non-governmental organisations.
A foreign ministry spokesman told reporters the meeting had been organised without consulting Pakistan and that some delegates had no right to attend such a conference.
He took particular objection to India, which he said did not figure in the list of donors to Afghanistan.

"We have now learnt that the venue of the conference has been shifted to Geneva," he said. "We also understand that India is still on the list of invitees and we will convey to the UNDP and the United Nations our reservations on India's participation in this conference."
But the spokesman said Pakistan, as an important donor for Afghanistan, would attend the Geneva meeting despite its objections.
Last month, Pakistan boycotted an Iran-proposed regional conference on Afghanistan in Tehran to which India was invited.
Pakistan is averse to giving any role to India in the Afghan problem on the grounds that it does not share borders with Afghanistan and did not oppose Soviet occupation of the country in the 1980s.

Pakistan and India have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir, where New Delhi is fighting a Moslem separatist revolt in two-thirds of the region under its control.
